episode.title: Preserve paired tool-call identifiers for protocol versions that require them
episode.before: At parent 786c76cb76bea452fa7287cc1014c4a3d3cad2b1, the shared Google message converter treated only model IDs beginning with `claude-` or `gpt-oss-` as requiring explicit tool-call IDs. Consequently, Gemini 3 history serialization omitted IDs from both function-call parts and their corresponding function-response parts, even though the internal history contained matching tool-call identifiers.
episode.after: At cbaca60389f5d7097a43c95f56a19d344ecf2195, the requirement predicate also recognizes parsed Gemini major versions greater than or equal to 3. Existing converter branches governed by that predicate therefore emit the same normalized identifiers on function-call and function-response parts for Gemini 3 across the Google Generative AI and Vertex adapters, while Gemini 2.5 continues omitting them.
episode.diff: The implementation adds the existing Gemini major-version parser to `requiresToolCallId`, extending the predicate by one condition without changing the serialization branches. Tests add paired tool results, verify IDs on both sides of two tool interactions for multiple Gemini 3 model IDs and both adapter APIs, verify omission for Gemini 2.5, and directly test the expanded predicate while retaining prior Claude and GPT-OSS behavior.

evidence_units.claim: Commit cbaca603 is titled `fix(ai): preserve Gemini 3 tool call IDs (#7494)`, has parent 786c76cb, and modifies the shared converter and its Gemini 3 test file.
In the parent, `requiresToolCallId` returns true only for model IDs beginning with `claude-` or `gpt-oss-`; Gemini model IDs are not included.
The shared converter uses `requiresToolCallId(model.id)` when serializing assistant tool calls, conditionally adding `functionCall.id` from the internal tool-call block.
evidence_units.source: git show cbaca60389f5d7097a43c95f56a19d344ecf2195:packages/ai/src/api/google-shared.ts, `convertMessages`, assistant `toolCall` branch around line 176

evidence_units.claim: The same predicate controls whether a tool-result message contributes its matching `toolCallId` as `functionResponse.id`.
evidence_units.source: git show cbaca60389f5d7097a43c95f56a19d344ecf2195:packages/ai/src/api/google-shared.ts, `convertMessages`, tool-result branch around lines 215-222

evidence_units.claim: The Google Generative AI and Google Vertex request builders both pass model and conversation context through the shared `convertMessages` implementation.
evidence_units.source: git show cbaca60389f5d7097a43c95f56a19d344ecf2195:packages/ai/src/api/google-generative-ai.ts around line 360; packages/ai/src/api/google-vertex.ts around line 459

evidence_units.claim: Before serialization, `transformMessages` maintains a mapping from normalized tool-call IDs to tool-result IDs, preserving correlation when identifier normalization changes an ID.
The implementation extends `requiresToolCallId` with `getGeminiMajorVersion(modelId) !== undefined && geminiMajorVersion >= 3`; no separate Gemini-specific serialization path is introduced.

The integration-style parameterized test supplies two tool calls and two matching tool results, then expects both serialized function-call IDs and function-response IDs to equal `call_1` and `call_2` for Gemini 3 through Google Generative AI and Vertex histories.
evidence_units.source: git show cbaca60389f5d7097a43c95f56a19d344ecf2195:packages/ai/test/google-shared-gemini3-unsigned-tool-call.test.ts, test `preserves tool call IDs for $id via $api history`

evidence_units.claim: The compatibility test expects two Gemini 2.5 function calls and two function responses to remain present while all four serialized IDs remain undefined.
evidence_units.source: git show cbaca60389f5d7097a43c95f56a19d344ecf2195:packages/ai/test/google-shared-gemini3-unsigned-tool-call.test.ts, test `does not add a thoughtSignature for non-Gemini-3 models`

evidence_units.claim: The direct predicate test expects false for Gemini 2.5 and true for Gemini 3.6, Claude, and GPT-OSS model IDs.

The changed test file provides a validation ladder covering the classification boundary, paired request/response serialization, both consuming adapters, multiple tool interactions, and the older-version exclusion.

candidate_workflows.name: restore-versioned-tool-call-correlation
candidate_workflows.title: Restore tool-call correlation at a versioned protocol boundary
candidate_workflows.description: Repair structured history conversion when a newer protocol generation requires explicit identifiers on both tool calls and their responses, without changing older-version wire behavior.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure every tool call and corresponding tool result retain a matching explicit identifier when the target protocol version requires correlation IDs.
when_to_use: A conversation adapter receives internally correlated tool calls and results but emits structured history without their identifiers.
The requirement begins at an identifiable model or protocol version boundary.
One shared capability predicate already controls both call-side and response-side ID serialization.
anti_goals: Do not add IDs unconditionally to older protocol versions whose established wire representation omits them.
Do not create separate provider-specific conversion paths when both adapters consume the shared converter.
Do not alter thought-signature handling, tool payloads, or result content while repairing identifier correlation.
not_applicable_when: The internal history lacks stable identifiers linking tool results to tool calls.
Only one side of the external protocol accepts an identifier and paired call-response equality is not its contract.
The affected adapters do not share the capability predicate or serialization boundary.
inputs: Version parser or equivalent capability metadata
Conversation history with tool calls and matching tool results
Representative older and newer version cases
workflow_graph.entry_state: A newer protocol generation is routed through a shared converter, but the capability predicate excludes it, so call and response IDs are dropped during replay.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The required protocol generation emits matching IDs on every serialized function call and function response through each shared adapter, while the tested older generation continues omitting IDs.

steps.condition: The ID requirement can be expressed as a stable family or major-version capability boundary.
steps.validation: Direct boundary cases return the expected capability result without regressing previously supported families.

steps.condition: Both function-call and function-response serialization consult the shared capability decision.
steps.validation: A multi-call history produces equal ordered IDs on call and response parts for every consuming adapter, and produces no IDs for the excluded older version.

validation_ladder: Unit-check the capability predicate immediately below and above the version boundary.
Serialize at least two tool calls and matching results to detect missing, duplicated, or reordered correlation IDs.
Assert equality of call-side and response-side identifier sequences.
Run the same history through every adapter that consumes the shared converter.
Assert an older protocol version preserves its prior omission behavior.
Retain unrelated structured-message assertions, including thought-signature behavior.
stop_conditions: Stop if the protocol's explicit-ID requirement cannot be established from implementation or tests.
Stop if internal tool results cannot be mapped to their originating calls.
Stop if enabling the capability changes older-version serialization.
Stop if only call IDs or only response IDs survive the conversion.
